summary: What each released version of the desktop app can do, so an assistant knows which steps it can hand to the app and when to tell the user to update. The app performs every transaction; this MCP server only reads.
resolving_a_version: An entry is keyed by the version that introduced its capability set. A version carrying "capabilities_as" behaves exactly as the entry it names, with the fixes in its "changes" list; a version with no entry at all behaves as the newest entry at or below it.

changes: a relay that never completes is sent once more rather than failing the probe: the first relay into a session the supplier's relayer has only just joined can arrive truncated, which read as a broken service. Any HTTP answer, a 5xx included, is still graded as it stands
the session check says when a session is at most a block old, since being in a session is not the same as the relayer having caught up with it
preflight folds to a green "Preflight passed" line once the action it cleared is running
funding a wallet and returning POKT to the owner narrate their progress in the window instead of falling silent until the transaction lands

capabilities_added: unstake an application (begin unbonding), signed by the application wallet itself, in the app window; the app shows the live unbonding period and the block the stake returns at, and staking again before then cancels it
return an application wallet's POKT to the owner wallet, the counterpart of funding one; the destination is always the imported owner wallet and cannot be chosen
electron-0.1.5.not_on_the_bridge: tx-unstake-app and tx-return-to-owner are deliberately app-window only and have no psm_ tools: one starts a wait that cannot be shortened, the other empties a wallet. Tell the user to do them in Stake application and in Wallets.
changes: a screen opened from a row or from a fix-this link offers a way back to where the user came from

capabilities_added: unstake an application (begin unbonding), signed by the application wallet itself, in the app window; the app shows the live unbonding period and the block the stake returns at, and staking again before then cancels it
electron-0.1.4.not_on_the_bridge: tx-unstake-app is deliberately app-window only and has no psm_ tool: unbonding starts a wait that cannot be shortened, so it is taken at the screen rather than handed to an assistant. Tell the user to do it in Stake application.
changes: a screen opened from a row or from a fix-this link offers a way back to where the user came from

a stake whose verification does not confirm is reported as what actually went wrong: the record could not be read, the stake on chain is below what was submitted, or a service is neither active nor scheduled. A service scheduled for the next session boundary is success, named with its activation block, not a failure
the record is re-read past the cache, and once more if the node does not answer, so one unlucky request no longer reads as a stake that did not take

Test service refuses to run until the node reports a supplier serving the service in the current session, and names the block the wait ends at: a stake joins at a session boundary, never the moment it is signed
the Test screen's bad-input probe sends malformed JSON instead of an empty object, which a service whose fields are all optional answers 200 to, correctly
Create and Register pick a service folder with the platform folder dialog, so a folder made outside the app no longer needs a restart to appear

local_mcp_bridge.transport: MCP Streamable HTTP, JSON responses, POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp (default port 41777), Authorization: Bearer <per-install token>
local_mcp_bridge.enabled_by: Settings, Claude Integration, Turn on (off by default); the same panel shows the token and the claude mcp add command
local_mcp_bridge.confirmation: every spend or signature opens a confirmation in the app window and waits for the user (typed token on MainNet); dry: true previews the command without confirmation
local_mcp_bridge.never_available: owner key import and revoke, application wallet create, recover, import, export: no key or phrase ever crosses the bridge
local_mcp_bridge.servers: named by their Settings entry; SSH key paths never cross the bridge

capabilities: everything in hta-2026-09-14, rebuilt in Electron with the same screens
one-time import of the HTA's settings, wallet records, activity, and keyring passphrase on the same PC
not_available: no silent auto-update: the app checks the latest release, shows a header link, and installs on click (Scoop, verified installer, or verified portable download)
Windows only; the macOS app is a separate product

capabilities: application wallets: create, recover, import, fund, export, remove
delegate an application to a gateway chosen from the live gateway list, and undelegate
settings: services folder, SSH server entries (a server is network-agnostic)
provision one supplier stack per network per server (HA RelayMiner in its own directory, operator key created on the server, one public hostname per network, shared Caddy per server)
deploy a service backend to a provisioned server and connect it to that network's relayer
unstake supplier (signed by the owner wallet; the app shows the live unbonding period and the return block, and an unstaking supplier shows as unstaking until the stake returns)
service lifecycle status per network: created, registered, pending (with the activation block), active
test relays through the protocol with pocket-ap
not_available: no local MCP bridge: the assistant guides the user through the app's buttons rather than driving them

electron-keyring-bundle.notes: encrypted keyring export/import for moving between machines
